climate.overview_html: The EU Joint Research Centre reports over 505,000 hectares burned across Europe in 2026, already ahead of 2025's pace, as compounding drought and heat drive unprecedented fire conditions. A new Geophysical Research Letters analysis by Foster & Rahmstorf confirms global warming has accelerated to 0.35°C per decade since 2015 — nearly double the 1970–2015 rate — placing the Paris 1.5°C ceiling before 2030. The WMO ASO-2026 seasonal update forecasts a record-smashing El Niño averaging +2.9°C sea-surface anomaly through October, and the Balkans heatwave linked to over 28,000 EU excess deaths has finally ended.

items.headline: Europe 2026: 505,000+ Hectares Burned, Rivers at Record Lows as Drought and Heat Compound
items.summary: Wildfire burnt area already exceeds 2025 pace. Loire, Po, Rhine, and Danube at record-low flows. Extreme fire danger stretches from Germany through Poland to the Balkans.

items.headline: Record El Niño Could Fast-Forward Planet's Temperature by a Decade
items.summary: WMO forecasts +2.9°C Pacific SST anomaly for ASO 2026. Combination with El Niño, hot ocean waters, and jet-stream changes temporarily pushes global temps to late-2030s levels.

items.headline: Scientists Confirm Sharp Acceleration in Global Warming Since 2015
items.summary: Foster & Rahmstorf (Geophysical Research Letters) find 0.35°C/decade since 2015 vs. 0.2°C/decade in prior decades — with >98% statistical confidence. Paris 1.5°C limit on track before 2030.

items.headline: August 2026 Tracking as Third-Warmest August on Record Globally
items.summary: SW Europe posts its most intense August heat anomaly in the ERA5 record back to 1940.

items.headline: 11-Year Streak of Record Global Warming Continues — 2026 Among Four Hottest Years
items.summary: 2015–2025 confirmed as the hottest 11-year period on record. 2026 projected comparable to 2023–2025, approaching the 2024 record at 1.55°C above pre-industrial baseline.

items.headline: Arctic Winter Sea-Ice Extent Sets New Record Low for 2026
items.summary: Winter maximum reached 13.76 million km² on March 13 — narrowly below 2025's record. Second consecutive year at record low; Sea of Okhotsk and Baffin Bay both anomalously open.

items.headline: Balkans Heatwave Fully Ends — All Heat Alerts Lifted Across EU
items.summary: Episode attributed to over 28,000 EU excess deaths since June — deadliest since 2003. All major heat alerts now lifted as Atlantic trough breaks pattern.

items.headline: Extraordinary August 2026 ENSO Diagnostic: Subsurface Pacific Heat Reaches +10°C
items.summary: 69% probability the 2026/27 El Niño exceeds every prior event since 1950 in peak amplitude.

major_events.name: Hurricane Lala — Central Pacific
major_events.impact: Re-intensified; threatens NW Hawaiian atolls with dangerous surf and inundation beginning Wednesday UTC.

major_events.name: Tropical Depression 17W (Saudel) — Near Guam
major_events.impact: Rapidly organizing at low latitude with minimal wind shear; super-typhoon potential flagged by JTWC.

major_events.name: US South Heat Dome — Texas to Carolinas
major_events.impact: Heat indices 110–115°F through August 21; dozens of daily and all-time records threatened across TX, GA, SC, FL panhandle.

weather.overview_html: Hurricane Lala (CAT 2, 110 mph) re-intensified in the central Pacific and threatens the NW Hawaiian atolls with dangerous surf beginning Wednesday. Near Guam, Tropical Depression 17W is rapidly organizing and is expected to reach typhoon strength by Thursday, with super-typhoon potential in a low-shear, deep-tropics environment. In the US, a dangerous heat dome is baking 70+ million people from Texas to the Carolinas with heat indices topping 115°F.

items.headline: Hurricane Lala Reaches Category 2 With 110-MPH Winds in Central Pacific
items.summary: NW Hawaiian atolls face dangerous surf and inundation threat beginning Wednesday UTC. Track forecast to curve northwest, keeping landfall risk to uninhabited atolls.

items.headline: Tropical Depression 17W Rapidly Organizing Near Guam — Super-Typhoon Potential
items.summary: Classic El Niño deep-tropics system; typhoon status expected by Thursday. Minimal wind shear and record-warm SSTs support rapid intensification. 2026 season's Sinlaku already set 905 hPa record.

items.headline: US South Heat Dome: 70+ Million Under Alerts as Heat Indices Top 115°F
items.summary: Heat indices peak 110–115°F from Memphis to the Florida Panhandle, coastal South Carolina, and southern Georgia. Dozens of records threatened through August 21.

items.headline: 2026 North American Heat Wave: Ongoing — Texas, Midwest, Southeast All Affected
items.summary: Multi-week heat event driven by a persistent upper-level ridge. Combination of El Niño-boosted background temperatures and a stalled synoptic pattern producing duration records as well as intensity records.

items.headline: Europe's Heatwave Fuels Drought, Wildfires and Record-Low River Levels
items.summary: Danube, Rhine, Loire, and Po at historically low levels. Shipping and hydropower generation disrupted. Wildfire smoke measured across much of western and central Europe.

renewables.overview_html: The Trump administration's $1.22B settlement with RWE — the fifth US offshore wind buyout, now totaling $3.9B in public funds — contrasts with a record 43.4 GW of US utility-scale solar PV forecast for 2026. Grid-scale battery storage is surging but stalling in interconnection queues as transformer and switchgear lead times stretch.

items.headline: Trump Pays RWE $1.22B to Cancel US Offshore Wind Leases — Fifth Buyout, $3.9B Total
items.summary: RWE relinquishes leases off New York, New Jersey, northern California, and the Gulf of Mexico — ~7 GW capacity. In exchange, RWE redirects investment to Louisiana LNG. Interior Dept. total offshore wind buyouts now $3.9B.

items.headline: Revolution Wind Now 95% Complete — 61 of 65 Turbines Installed Off Connecticut
items.summary: Final four turbines on track to close out before year-end, bringing the project to full commercial operation and delivering on a $2.9B development first announced in 2019.

items.headline: US Big Battery Projects Pile Up as Grid Upgrade Delays Stall Interconnection
items.summary: Con Edison reports 300% growth in storage projects awaiting connection over two years. LFP cell prices at $55–75/kWh — below most analyst expectations — but transformer shortages, not economics, are the primary bottleneck.

items.headline: EIA Forecasts Record 43.4 GW US Utility-Scale Solar PV Additions in 2026
items.summary: A 60% year-on-year jump driven by falling panel costs and accelerating corporate clean-power demand from data centers. Wind expected to provide ~11% of 2026 US generation; solar ~8%.

items.headline: Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners Closes Growth Markets Fund II at $3B
items.summary: Nearly triple its predecessor fund. Targets solar, wind, storage, and grid infrastructure across 15 emerging economies. Largest dedicated emerging-market clean-energy close of 2026.

science.overview_html: The peer-reviewed version of ECMWF's AIFS 1.1.0 appears in Geoscientific Model Development, showing 4–6% skill gains and major precipitation improvements from hard physical constraints. Foster & Rahmstorf (GRL) confirm warming has accelerated to 0.35°C/decade since 2015 with >98% confidence. Ocean heat content in 2025 rose another 24 ZJ above 2024, a new record. Allen Institute's ACE2 matches physics-based seasonal forecast skill at 1,000× less compute.

items.headline: State of the Climate in 2025: Record Greenhouse Gases, Sea Level, and Ocean Heat
items.summary: 2025 ranks among the three warmest years since 1850 despite a fading La Niña. Every major climate indicator — CO₂, CH₄, sea level, ocean heat — set new records for the second consecutive year.

items.headline: Rate of Warming, Not Just Temperature Level, Determines AMOC Collapse Risk
items.summary: Slow CO₂ ramps keep AMOC stable to +5.5°C; fast ramps collapse it at +2°C. Finding reframes risk assessment: stabilization rate and trajectory matter as much as endpoint temperature.

items.headline: AIFS Single 1.1.0: Formal Validation of ECMWF's Machine-Learned Weather Forecast Model
items.summary: Hard physical-consistency constraints in training substantially improve precipitation skill. Soil and energy-flux variables added. Consistent 4–6% improvements across lead times and variables vs. AIFS 1.0.

items.headline: Global Warming Has Accelerated Significantly Since 2015
items.summary: After removing ENSO, volcanic, and solar signals from five major datasets, warming rate of 0.35°C/decade since 2015 is confirmed with >98% confidence — ~75% faster than 1970–2015. At this pace, long-term 1.5°C exceedance before 2030.

items.headline: Ocean Heat Content Sets Another Record in 2025 — Up 24 ZJ Above 2024
items.summary: Full-depth global ocean heat content rose 481 ± 48 ZJ above 1960 baseline. About 33% of global ocean area ranked in top-3 warmest years; tropical Atlantic and Mediterranean especially anomalous.

items.headline: Arctic Winter Sea Ice Sets Another Record Low Maximum in 2026
items.meta: National Snow and Ice Data Center
items.summary: Annual maximum 13.76 million km² on March 13 — edge below 2025 record, second consecutive year at satellite-era record low. Sea of Okhotsk and Baffin Bay both anomalously open.

items.headline: Global Ocean Heat Monitoring Critically Dependent on Argo Float Network Density
items.summary: Sampling gaps in the Southern Ocean and tropical Pacific introduce up to 15% uncertainty in decadal heat-content estimates. Paper calls for expanded Argo deployment and better coverage metrics in IPCC reporting.

items.source: Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems (AIES)
items.headline: Severe Weather Forecasts from AI Weather Prediction Models: Skill Comparable to ML-Guidance Products
items.summary: Random forests applied to AI model outputs achieve 1–8-day severe weather prediction skill on par with existing operational ML products. AI models (GraphCast, AIFS) lag on extreme precipitation and convective initiation but perform well on large-scale dynamics.

items.headline: ACE2 ML Emulator Matches Physics-Based Seasonal Forecast Skill at 1,000× Less Compute
items.summary: Ai2's ACE2 atmospheric emulator achieves wintertime NAO correlation ~0.5, comparable to physics-based ensembles. Stable 100-year simulations capture MJO and ENSO variability. 4-month seasonal forecast in 2 minutes on a single GPU.

items.title: WindBorne Systems Raises $37M Series B — Claims World's Most Accurate Weather Forecast Model
items.body_html: WindBorne Systems closed a $37M Series B co-led by Khosla Ventures and Galvanize (valuation: $250M, total raised: $62M+). The company operates over 600 autonomous long-duration sensing balloons and feeds proprietary atmospheric profiles into its WeatherMesh-6 model, which it claims beats ECMWF HRES, GFS, and rival AI models on public benchmarks. Proceeds fund balloon constellation expansion and next-generation model development.

items.title: Base Power Raises $1B Series D at $13B Valuation to Scale Backyard Battery Network
items.body_html: Base Power raised another $1B less than a year after its previous billion-dollar round, reaching a $13B post-money valuation. The Austin-based company installs ~100 home batteries per day in Texas and Illinois, aggregating them into a virtual power plant. It simultaneously launched the Base Core, a 39.2 kWh home battery manufactured in Texas — significantly larger than competitors' units.

items.title: MSCI Completes $120M Acquisition of First Street to Expand Physical Climate Risk Analytics
items.body_html: MSCI closed its acquisition of First Street, a climate risk data provider with flood, wildfire, hurricane, and heat models covering 2.4B+ structures worldwide. The $120M cash deal (announced June 24, closed August 3) integrates First Street's physical hazard layer into MSCI's institutional investor and real-estate analytics suite. Additional earnout payments are contingent on two-year revenue performance.

items.title: Form Energy Raises $750M Series G to Scale Iron-Air Battery Manufacturing
items.body_html: Form Energy, maker of 100-hour iron-air batteries, closed a $750M Series G led by T. Rowe Price, with Sequoia and Franklin Templeton joining. Total equity raised past $2B. Commercial backlog quadrupled in 2026 to 80 GWh, including contracts with Xcel Energy and Google.

items.title: H1 2026 Climate Tech VC Hits $26B — Up 55% — as Data Center Power Demand Drives Surge
items.body_html: Climate tech venture funding reached $26.1B in H1 2026, up 55% vs. H1 2025 and the strongest first-half since 2022. Data center-related technologies claimed 34% of all climate funding — up from just 3% the prior year. Capital concentrated into fewer companies: average round size jumped to $27M, while total deal count hit a record low, per ESG Today.

items.title: All Aboard Coalition — $60B VC Alliance — Backs $300M Fund for Climate-Tech Scale-Up
items.body_html: A consortium of VC and PE firms managing $60B in assets launched a $300M fund to bridge the pilot-to-commercial gap for climate-tech startups, targeting energy storage, carbon removal, and grid technology. The vehicle focuses on companies that have proven technology but lack the capital for first commercial deployments — the "valley of death" stage that has stalled many 2022–2024 cohort companies.
